findings.title: Safe mode forgets owner_user_ids, so any option error opens the dashboard, private diagnostics and controls to every Home Assistant user
findings.evidence: config.py:404-408 `_safe_mode` returns `Settings(dry_run=True)`, which is all built-in defaults, including `owner_user_ids=()`. main.py:113-115 builds `AccessPolicy(owner_ids=loaded.settings.owner_user_ids)` from those defaults. security.py:100 `is_owner` then returns True for everyone (`not self.owner_ids`). Any validation error triggers this: the cross-field rules (config.py:288-299) or a bound that only config.py enforces (see config-bounds-only-in-python). The diagnostics are not limited to dry-run data: diagnostics.py:474 and :559 read the ledger and cycles of every mode. The dashboard then shows the 'Everyone ... counts as its owner, put your ID in owner_user_ids' banner (app.js:741-745), so the owner is told to set an option they already set. Live: the owner relies on this option (0.13.0 report OPTIONS:74-76, owner_user_ids = [7f32…]).
findings.failure_scenario: The owner follows the first analysis (§0.4) and raises min_sleep_minutes to 180 but leaves wake_interval_minutes at 60 (live values in the 0.13.0 report). Home Assistant accepts each field, but config.py:292 refuses the pair, so on restart Ember runs in safe mode. Until the owner notices and fixes it, any other Home Assistant user (a family admin, a wall tablet's account) can open the panel. They can download the private diagnostics with other people's emails and web text, pause, grant money, send messages or use the kill switch (the kill switch is global, economy/life.py:55).
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/test_safe_mode_owner.py. With options {owner_user_ids:[OWNER], site_url:'http://my-shop.example'} it printed `safe_mode: True ... owner_user_ids: ()`. As a non-owner (TABLET): `GET dashboard: 200`, `GET diagnostics full: 200`, `POST pause: 200 {"state":"paused"}`. A second test first recorded a live grant as the owner, then restarted with the typo: `SAFE MODE tablet diagnostics: 200 live grant visible: True`. daily_spend_cap_usd 0.4 (below the default cycle cap) and a 61-character site_name also gave safe_mode True with owner_user_ids ().
findings.related: 0.3 (owner_user_ids, af0f19a); §10 'Don't ship the policy engine before owner identity is enforced'
findings.fix: Fail closed. In `_safe_mode`, parse `owner_user_ids` (and `kill_switch_reset`) from the raw options with their own validators and keep them. If they can't be parsed, deny everyone except a page that names the safe mode and the caller's user ID. Name what safe mode resets in the safe-mode banner. Add a test: owner IDs survive an unrelated invalid option.

findings.title: A safe-mode start lifts an engaged kill switch whenever kill_switch_reset isn't 0, and the live agent then runs after the owner fixes the options
findings.evidence: main.py:154 always calls `apply_kill_switch_reset(database, economy, loaded.settings.kill_switch_reset)`. In safe mode the value is the default 0 (config.py:155, :408). owner.py:895-908 compares it with the stored marker: when they differ it stores the new value and, if the agent is killed, lifts the kill (`set_switch(KILLED_KEY, False)`). KILLED_KEY is one global meta flag (economy/life.py:55, :474-477), not per mode. The next valid start then sees the owner's real value differ from the stored '0' and moves the marker back without re-killing. The same path also lifts a kill made during safe mode.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner once reset a kill (kill_switch_reset = 1). Later Ember overspends, so they use the kill switch and go to Configuration to tighten the options. Setting the daily cap below the cycle cap puts Ember in safe mode on restart. The System log reads 'The kill switch was reset in the options; the agent may run again'. The owner corrects the cap and restarts. Ember is now live and alive with every unlock still standing (see kill-switch-keeps-unlocks), although the owner never changed kill_switch_reset.
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/test_safe_mode_owner.py::test_live_data_and_kill_in_safe_mode. Live start with kill_switch_reset 1, then the owner's kill: `owner kill: 200 {'state': 'killed'}`. Restart with an http site_url: `SAFE MODE killed flag: False state: alive`, with events 'The kill switch was reset in the options; the agent may run again'. Restart with the fixed options: `LIVE AGAIN killed flag: False state: alive`.
findings.related: 0.3 / kill switch (DOCS.md:905-907 'stops the agent for good ... to undo it, change Kill switch reset')
findings.fix: Don't call apply_kill_switch_reset in safe mode, or carry the raw kill_switch_reset over (as in safe-mode-drops-owner-identity). Only store the reset marker from valid options. Add a regression test: killed, safe-mode start, valid start: still killed.

findings.title: The kill switch doesn't take back the owner's unlocks: on reset, requests held in a veto window are approved and carried out at once
findings.evidence: owner.py:874-892 `kill` only sets KILLED_KEY. `policy.revoke_all` (policy.py:415) is called only by take_back_unlocks (owner.py:600-616). While killed, run_policy returns early (service.py:715-716), and held requests stay pending. After a reset, `policy.run_due` approves every held request whose 12-hour window has passed, and execute_approved carries it out in the same scheduler round (scheduler.py:84-90). The first analysis's Phase D item 'a kill switch that revokes every class' is struck through as done with 110f71a (analysis line 796), but the code puts it on a separate button.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner has a veto_window unlock for price changes. Ember proposes a 10% cut and the change is held. Alarmed by other behaviour, the owner kills Ember instead of vetoing each held item. Days later they reset the kill switch, and the held price change is approved by 'Ember's code (your unlock)' and pushed to Etsy in the first round, without the owner seeing it again.
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/test_kill_held.py printed: `held request: pending`; `kill: {'state': 'killed'}`; `grants after kill: [{'rule': 'price_change', 'level': 'veto_window'}]`; `while killed: [{'status': 'pending'}]`; `after reset: [{'status': 'approved', 'decided_by': "Ember's code (your unlock)"}]`; `carried out: [(3, 'done')] price 4.50 -> 4.05`.
findings.related: Phase D audit (110f71a): 'a kill switch that revokes every class'
findings.fix: In `kill`, call `policy.revoke_all(..., why='the kill switch')` in the same transaction, and add the owner's note per milestone as take_back does. Say so in the kill dialog. Add a test: kill, then reset, then held requests wait for the owner.

findings.title: Undo is accepted and promised for 'the next round' while Ember is paused, killed or unfunded, but it never runs until the agent is alive again
findings.evidence: owner.undo (owner.py:618-636) and audit.undo create an approved request with no check of the life state. execute_approved returns [] whenever `executor_blocked()` (service.py:690-697, :729-730) finds a state other than alive or critical. The UI then says 'Undo requested: request #N, carried out in the next round.' (app.js:2255). The request card shows execution 'waiting' with no reason (etsy_publisher.edit_execution:212-227). DOCS.md:842-852 describes Undo without this limit, and DOCS.md:903-904 says Pause 'stops and restarts the wake cycles', not that it stops every executor.
findings.failure_scenario: An automatic listing change goes wrong. The owner hits Pause (or the kill switch), the natural first move, then presses Undo: the listing stays changed or active on Etsy indefinitely, while the dashboard says the Undo happens in the next round. If they resume days later, the stale 'change it back' runs then and may overwrite edits they made by hand at Etsy in the meantime (inferred).
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/test_undo_killed.py. Killed: `undo request: 3`, `execute_approved while killed: [] blocked: The agent is killed`, `listing state: active`. Paused: `execute_approved: [] blocked: The agent is paused state: active`.
findings.fix: Let owner-initiated Undo requests (linked in action_undos) run while paused or unfunded, since they spend no API money: an executor path that ignores the life state for them. While killed, refuse the Undo with a clear 409 (or run it too, which the owner asked for). Say in the card and the status line when an approved request waits because the agent is paused or killed.

findings.title: The open REST-sensor JSON (/api/sensors, no user needed) carries the daily digest, which can contain the email address of a person who asked to stop
findings.evidence: policy.py:345 sets the revocation reason to `f"{stopped['address']} asked to stop after an automatic reply (request #N)"`, stored in policy_grants.why. audit.py:462-466 copies `t['why']` into the digest text, and service.py:863 puts `digest['text']` into sensor_fields. /api/sensors is in OPEN_PATHS (security.py:52): any Home Assistant user can read it through Ingress whatever owner_user_ids says, and any host-network process can read it from 172.30.32.1 (security.py:114). Both security.py:10 ('only ever contains non-sensitive numbers') and DOCS.md:1606-1609 (suggests an automation that notifies on the digest) promise otherwise. The diagnostics mask addresses (privacy.py) but the sensor does not.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner unlocks email_reply. Ember auto-answers a customer, and the customer replies 'stop'. The kill rule revokes the unlock. Next morning the digest reads '... (lena.hoffmann@example.org asked to stop after an automatic reply ...)'. The address of someone who opted out is now in the unauthenticated sensor JSON, in Home Assistant's recorder history if the owner set up the suggested sensor and automation, and in phone notifications.
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/test_digest_sensor.py reuses tests/test_inquiries.py's opt-out test, advances a day and runs run_policy. `sensor_fields()['digest']` printed '... Unlocks taken back: email replies in threads the other person started for milestone #4 (lena.hoffmann@example.org asked to stop after an automatic reply (request #1)).' and `third-party address in the open sensor JSON: True`.
findings.related: 0.3 open paths; Phase D daily digest (110f71a); Phase E1 kill rule (1a8ad44)
findings.fix: Never put an address in `why`: write 'the person you answered in request #N asked to stop'. Also run digest text through privacy masking before it reaches the sensor and events, or expose only digest_day and counts in /api/sensors. Add a test that the sensor JSON contains no '@'.

findings.title: Autonomy unlocks (auto email replies, price changes) can be granted while owner identity isn't enforced
findings.evidence: owner.set_autonomy (owner.py:560-599) and POST /api/milestones/{id}/autonomy (web.py:575-582) don't check that owner_user_ids is set. With the option empty (the default, config.yaml:84), or in safe mode (safe-mode-drops-owner-identity), security.py:100 treats every panel user as the owner. The first analysis made this a precondition: '0.3 ... This has to land before any autonomy is delegated' and §10 'Don't ship the policy engine before owner identity is enforced'. The 0.13.0 policy engine shipped with identity optional.
findings.failure_scenario: A new install, or this owner's install during a safe-mode start. A second Home Assistant admin or a shared tablet session sets email_reply and price_change to 'auto' with 20 a day and a budget of 100. Ember then emails people and changes Etsy prices without the owner's click. The audit shows the tablet's name, but only after the fact.
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/test_unlock_without_identity.py (default settings; a user 'Wall tablet'): `email_reply -> 200 {... 'level': 'auto', 'per_day': 20, 'budget': 100}`, `price_change -> 200 {...}`, `owner banner ids_set: False`.
findings.related: 0.3 (af0f19a); Phase D policy engine (c5c3fb6); first analysis §10
findings.fix: Refuse any level other than manual (409 with a clear message) unless owner_user_ids is set or in dev mode. Also have policy.run_due ignore grants while identity isn't enforced, so a later safe mode can't use existing grants. Show the reason on the Autonomy panel.

findings.title: The Inbox shows only the newest 30 messages: an older message of the owner's can't be read, checked for an answer or removed from the dashboard
findings.evidence: views.py:183 builds the inbox from `store.queue(conn, 'messages', scope)`, and store.py:521-525 defaults to LIMIT 30. There is no GET route to page messages (web.py has only POST /api/inbox*). The only removal path is the button on a rendered inbox item (app.js:3240-3254 -> POST api/inbox/{id}/remove). Upgrades use the same 30-row window (views.py:202). FIX NOW 25 fixed this for approvals and the ledger but not for messages. Live: 63 messages after about 3 days (0.13.0 report DATABASE:158), so messages older than about 1.5 days are already out of reach.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner realises they pasted a password into a message two days ago (the case DOCS.md:884-887 and :1442-1450 describe). The message is no longer among the newest 30, so there is no Remove button: its text stays in the database, is not registered for redaction, and, if unanswered, keeps going to Anthropic in every plan. The owner also can't see whether an old question was ever answered.
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/test_inbox_window.py: one message with a password, then 34 more. It printed `sent: 35 shown: 30 oldest shown id: 6 first message shown: False`.
findings.related: FIX NOW 25 (5) approvals list; 0.2 message removal
findings.fix: Add GET /api/inbox?before= and a 'Show older messages' button, as for the ledger. Always include the owner's unanswered and unremoved messages whatever their age. Do the same for upgrades with status 'new'.

findings.title: 13 options are bounded (or pattern-checked) only in config.py, so a value the Supervisor accepts switches the whole agent to safe mode (dry run forced)
findings.evidence: config.yaml:158-160, 178, 188, 198-206 declare strategy/research/workshop_model, etsy_keystring, pinterest_app_id and site_name/url/owner_name/address/email/phone/vat_id/host as plain `str?`/`url?`/`email?`. config.py:133-134, 151, 176, 199, 217-225 give them max_length 20-300, and config.py:296-299 require site_url to be https with no query (`_SITE_URL`, config.py:32). tests/test_manifest.py:126-144 compares only `str(a,b)`/`int`/`float` rules, so none of these gaps are tested. Safe mode means all defaults and dry run (config.py:404-408), which contradicts config.py:161-162's own principle that a bad integration setting is 'reported by the integration, never by safe mode'. The translations (en.yaml site_url, site_name) mention none of these limits.
findings.failure_scenario: The owner turns the website on and enters `http://mein-shop.de` (Home Assistant's url type accepts http: inferred), a query-string address, an umlaut domain (`_SITE_URL` refuses `https://www.müller-shop.de`, checked) or a 61-character shop name. On restart the live agent silently becomes a dry-run agent with Etsy and email off until the owner reads the banner. The same start also triggers safe-mode-drops-owner-identity and safe-mode-lifts-kill-switch.
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/test_safe_mode_owner.py::test_cross_field_rule: `site_name 61 chars -> safe_mode: True ['site_name: String should have at most 60 characters']`. The http site_url case: `errors: ['options: Value error, site_url must be an https address ...']`. `_SITE_URL.match('https://www.müller-shop.de')` is False.
findings.fix: Move the bounds into config.yaml (`str(,60)?`, and `match(^https://...)?` for site_url, which the Supervisor supports), so bad values are refused at save time. Report bad site_* values on the Website card (status not_ready) instead of refusing the whole options file. Extend test_manifest to every '?' rule and to max_length metadata. Document the limits in en.yaml.

findings.title: The Ledger tab silently skips entries once new ones arrive after 'Show older entries' was used
findings.evidence: app.js:1446-1451 merges the poll's newest 20 entries (economy/service.py:410) with the loaded older pages (`ui.ledgerOlder`), dropping only duplicates. When more than 20 entries are booked between polls (every model call books entries; live ledger 446 rows after 46 cycles), the entries between the old newest-20 window and the new one are in neither list. Nothing marks the gap, and 'Show older' continues from the oldest loaded id (app.js:1501-1502).
findings.failure_scenario: The owner opens the Ledger, clicks Show older entries (ids 81-180 load under 181-200) and leaves the tab open while a wake cycle books 30 entries. The next poll shows 230..211 followed by 180..81: entries 210..181 (that cycle's API costs, or a grant recorded meanwhile) are missing without a sign, so a manual reconciliation against the page is wrong.
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/ledger_gap.js runs app.js's merge logic on that sequence and printed `after: shown 120 entries, first 230 last 81 missing ids 210..181 (30)`.
findings.fix: When older pages are loaded and the newest page no longer touches them (min newest id > max older id + 1), fetch the gap with GET api/ledger?before=<oldest newest id>&limit=500, or clear ui.ledgerOlder and show the button again. Add a UI unit test of the merge.

findings.title: A small .docx upload can make Ember allocate gigabytes (no uncompressed-size limit), and a malformed one returns a 500
findings.evidence: library.py:186-205 checks only the compressed size (FILE_BYTES 8 MB, :41). library.py:175-183 passes the bytes straight to `docx.Document`, which reads each zip part whole into memory. It catches only BadZipFile, KeyError and ValueError, so lxml's XMLSyntaxError (and docx PackageNotFoundError) escape owner.add_document (owner.py:718-721) and reach CatchAllMiddleware as a 500. XML entities are safe: python-docx parses with resolve_entities=False (docx/oxml/parser.py:19).
findings.failure_scenario: The owner uploads a 'guide.docx' downloaded from the web that is a zip bomb (about 1,000:1 compression). Near the 8 MB limit, python-docx tries to allocate about 15 GB. On a 4-8 GB Home Assistant box the kernel OOM-kills the app mid-cycle (the unfinished call is charged at its worst case on restart). Smaller bombs just return 'internal error' instead of 'this Word file can't be read'.
findings.label: reproduced
findings.reproduction: scratchpad/web/docx_bomb.py. A 425 KB upload (400 MB document.xml): `raised: XMLSyntaxError ...`, `time 6.4s, peak RSS 812 MB`. A 1.49 MB upload (1.5 GB): `peak RSS 2,926 MB`, time 21.1 s.
findings.fix: Before python-docx, open the zip, sum `ZipInfo.file_size` of the members, and refuse over about 50 MB or a ratio over 100 as a LibraryError. Catch lxml.etree.XMLSyntaxError and docx.opc.exceptions.PackageNotFoundError as 'this Word file can't be read'.

findings.title: Library uploads use the dashboard's 10-second request timeout, so an 8 MB file over remote access fails, possibly after the server stored it
findings.evidence: app.js:13 sets REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000 for every request (app.js:429-441), and the upload at app.js:6995 passes no timeout option. The diagnostics get their own 30 s (app.js:15). library.py:41 notes an 8 MB file travels as about 11 MB through Home Assistant's proxy. After the abort the UI says 'couldn't reach Ember', although the server may already have stored the document; a retry is then refused as a duplicate.
findings.failure_scenario: Through Nabu Casa or a phone connection at about 5 Mbit/s upstream, an 8 MB PDF (about 11 MB of base64) needs about 18 s, so every such upload aborts at 10 s. The patch note's '8 MB each' only works on the LAN.
findings.label: inferred
findings.fix: Pass {timeout: 120000} for library uploads (as for the diagnostics). When a request times out, re-check the library (loadLibrary) and say 'may have been added'.

fix_checks.item: 0.3: owner_user_ids enforced on every route (incl. routes added in 0.12/0.13)
fix_checks.evidence: SecurityMiddleware checks the first X-Remote-User-Id for every path except /static/*, /api/health and /api/sensors (security.py:97-103, :148-155), so every 0.12/0.13 route (autonomy, take_back, undo, knockouts, pinterest/*, site/*, library/*) is covered. Traversal probes (/static/../api/dashboard and encoded forms) gave 403/404 (scratchpad test_static_traversal). The live audit trail stores '[owner] ([id]…)' (0.13.0 report EVENTS:3457). But safe mode empties the option (finding safe-mode-drops-owner-identity), and unlocks don't require it (unlocks-without-owner-identity).

fix_checks.item: 0.3: open paths (health, sensors, static) hold nothing private
fix_checks.evidence: health returns version and database status only (web.py:112-115). Since 0.13.0, sensors includes the digest text (service.py:863), which can hold a third party's email address (finding sensor-digest-leaks-third-party-address).

fix_checks.item: CSRF: every state-changing route needs X-Ember-Request
fix_checks.evidence: security.py:145-147 refuses every non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS request without the header, and every new 0.12/0.13 route is a POST. app.js:437-441 sends the header on every non-GET. The only GET with a side effect is /api/site/download, which records the download (service.py:951-957); a cross-site request would need the session's ingress path and cookie (see notes).

fix_checks.item: FIX NOW 25 (4): Ledger tab 'Show older entries'
fix_checks.evidence: GET /api/ledger?before= works (web.py:214-223, ledger.py:473-483). The UI merge leaves a silent gap once new entries arrive (finding ledger-paging-gap, reproduced).

fix_checks.item: FIX NOW 25 (5): Approvals list every waiting/to-do request plus the newest 30 closed
fix_checks.evidence: store.approvals_for_owner (store.py:509-518) selects all pending/approved/approved_with_changes plus the newest 30 others, and views.py:131-161 uses it.

fix_checks.item: FIX NOW 25 (6): older Etsy orders that still need the owner stay listed
fix_checks.evidence: etsy_publisher.orders_json (etsy_publisher.py:1140-1196) reads up to 1,000 orders and returns the newest 20 plus every older recordable or refunded one. Measured: with 1,000 synthetic unrecorded orders the dashboard poll took 31 ms (5 ms without).

fix_checks.item: Phase D (dashboard): roadmap unlocks per milestone
fix_checks.evidence: The UI (app.js:6383-6430) and server validation (owner.py:560-599: rule, level, per_day ≤ 20, budget ≤ 100) work. The grant is allowed without enforced owner identity (finding unlocks-without-owner-identity).

It works while the agent is alive (tests/test_audit.py passes; one Undo at a time, newest action only). While paused, killed or unfunded it is accepted but never carried out, and the UI promises the next round (finding undo-blocked-while-paused-or-killed, reproduced).

fix_checks.item: Phase D: Take back every unlock
fix_checks.evidence: owner.take_back_unlocks (owner.py:600-616) calls policy.revoke_all and adds a note per milestone. POST /api/autonomy/take_back is at web.py:585-593, and the UI button with a confirm dialog at app.js:2268-2287.

fix_checks.item: Phase D plan item struck as done: 'a kill switch that revokes every class'
fix_checks.evidence: `kill` (owner.py:874-892) only sets KILLED_KEY, so unlocks survive a kill and fire on reset (finding kill-switch-keeps-unlocks, reproduced).

fix_checks.item: Phase D: daily digest on the card, System log and sensors
fix_checks.evidence: audit.write_due runs from run_policy (service.py:719-724). It appears on the card (app.js:2201-2203), in the sensor (service.py:862-863) and live ('Daily digest: 2026-09-29 …', 0.13.0 report EVENTS:3460). Privacy issue: see sensor-digest-leaks-third-party-address.

One connectArea (app.js:3706-3772). The authorize link is limited to www.etsy.com or www.pinterest.com (etsyLink/pinterestLink, app.js:3568-3582, 3795-3808). The server uses PKCE with a random state and a 15-minute window (pinterest_connection.py:78-107), and finish takes an address of at most 4,000 characters (web.py:377-379).

fix_checks.item: E3: website preview sandboxed on Home Assistant's origin
fix_checks.evidence: web.py:788 sends `sandbox allow-same-origin; default-src 'none'; style-src 'sha256-…'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'` without allow-scripts, forms or popups. Names are regex-limited (web.py:784), responses are nosniff, and the builder escapes every text with https/mailto links only (products/site.py:130-142, products/markup.py:39). test_site.py:253-277 passes.

fix_checks.item: E3: zip download, same bytes for the same site, recorded with SHA-256
fix_checks.evidence: test_site.py:133-134 (archive twice is equal); service.py:951-957 records the fingerprints. Note: the download is recorded before the bytes are delivered, on a GET.

fix_checks.item: E4: dashboard (Approved products group, Cancel, Record the cost)
fix_checks.evidence: The APPROVAL_GROUPS 'printing' group is at app.js:2162-2163. Cancel checks for a started product in the same transaction (owner.py:219-231). 'Record the cost' opens the expense form with an idempotency key per order (app.js:3950-3960).

POST /api/ventures/{id}/knockouts (web.py:565-572) goes to owner.override_knockout (owner.py:527-558): rule and boolean validated, 409 when nothing changes, history in knockout_overrides, and the owner's note on the venture. The UI is at app.js:5739-5770. tests/test_knockouts.py passes.

fix_checks.item: Library upload: 8 MB; txt/md/html/pdf/docx parsed without new dependencies
fix_checks.evidence: Types and size are enforced on the server (library.py:41, :186-205; owner.py:712-713). pypdfium2 and python-docx were already product dependencies. XML entity resolution is off, and a 400-page PDF parsed in 0.19 s. But the uncompressed .docx size is unbounded (docx-decompression-unbounded) and uploads use the 10 s timeout (library-upload-10s-timeout).

fix_checks.item: UI renders text only (enforced by a test)
fix_checks.evidence: A grep of app.js (7,145 lines) and theme.js found no innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval or javascript: sink. Every data-built href is validated: ownerLink (app.js:1829-1844), etsyLink, pinterestLink, redditLink (host-pinned), the library source regex (app.js:6822), and encodeURIComponent for workspace and site paths. The CSP has no unsafe-inline (security.py:62-68). test_web.py:367-381 enforces the sinks. It does not cover attribute sinks such as h(..., {href: data}): currently safe, but a guard would help.

fix_checks.item: config.py vs config.yaml vs translations consistency
fix_checks.evidence: Keys, defaults and str(a,b)/int/float bounds match and are tested (test_manifest.py:77-153, all pass), and the translations cover every key. 13 optional options are bounded only in config.py, and site_url and site_email carry patterns only there (finding config-bounds-only-in-python).

still_open_from_0_11_1: §9 packaging: no prebuilt images (config.yaml has no image:, so each device builds locally) and no hash-pinned installs (Dockerfile:17 `pip3 install --only-binary=:all: -r requirements.txt`, versions only, no --require-hashes).
§10 'Don't ship the policy engine before owner identity is enforced': the policy engine shipped with owner_user_ids optional (new, reproduced evidence in finding unlocks-without-owner-identity).

strengths.what: Default-deny owner check at the middleware, not per route
strengths.evidence: security.py:97-155: every path except /static/*, /api/health and /api/sensors needs an owner ID once the option is set. All 12 routes added in 0.12/0.13 were covered with no per-route code, and path-traversal probes returned 403/404 (scratchpad test_static_traversal). The owner set the option live (0.13.0 report OPTIONS:74-76), and events record '[owner] ([id]…)' (EVENTS:3457).

strengths.what: Text-only dashboard with validated links, enforced by a test
strengths.evidence: No HTML sink in 7,145 lines of app.js. Links are built only by validators that pin scheme and host (app.js:1829-1844, 2586-2599, 3568-3582, 3795-3808). The strict CSP has no unsafe-inline (security.py:62-68), and test_web.py:367-381 guards the sinks.

strengths.what: Every agent- or Ember-made file is served inert
strengths.evidence: Workspace text, products, upgrade scripts, the zip and the site preview all carry `sandbox` CSP, nosniff and no-store, as attachments except PNG/JPEG previews and the sandboxed site (web.py:695-838). Filenames are sanitized per RFC 6266/5987 (web.py:775-780). The preview runs no script on Home Assistant's origin.

proxy_headers=False, so the IP filter can't be spoofed (__main__.py:40). SUPERVISOR_TOKEN, proxies and ANTHROPIC_* env are removed before start (rootfs/.../ember/run). The container halts on exit so options are always re-read from the Supervisor (finish). hassio_api and homeassistant_api are false (config.yaml:24-26). The base image and all requirements are pinned, with wheels only. The vendored Chart.js checksum matches VENDORED.md (verified with sha256sum).

strengths.what: Optimistic concurrency and atomic cancels for owner decisions
strengths.evidence: Every approval update bumps `version` (owner.py:172-177, 234-238; policy.py:222; audit.py:365; all publishers). Cancel checks the executor's row in the same transaction (owner.py:195-231). The UI turns 409s into 'it changed meanwhile' and refreshes (app.js:2107-2126).

strengths.what: Parsers are safe against XML entities and cheap for PDFs
strengths.evidence: python-docx parses with resolve_entities=False (docx/oxml/parser.py:19). PDF text extraction stops at 2x the document limit (library.py:149-171); a 400-page PDF took 0.19 s.

strengths.what: Dashboard stays cheap as data grows
strengths.evidence: Measured: after 40 fake cycles (407 calls, 408 ledger rows) /api/dashboard was 103 KB and 13 ms. With 1,000 Etsy orders it was 31 ms. The tab data (ventures, roadmap, library) loads only when its stamp changes.

strengths.what: Options are never logged or shown in the clear
strengths.evidence: Every secret is a SecretStr registered for redaction (main.py:83-87, logging_setup.py:30-41). public_dict shows flags only (config.py:347-365). Validation errors never echo values (config.py:379-384). The config/manifest tests pass.

Every test in my area passes on HEAD: test_web, owner_identity, site, manifest, config, library, audit, knockouts, small_defects, owner_api, entrypoint, events and logging. The reproduction scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-SURVIVE/16767151-7117-55b8-8b14-a711cc61e9f8/scratchpad/web/ (test_safe_mode_owner.py, test_kill_held.py, test_undo_killed.py, test_digest_sensor.py, test_unlock_without_identity.py, test_inbox_window.py, ledger_gap.js, docx_bomb.py, and the timing scripts test_dashboard_load.py and test_orders_poll.py).

The two high findings share one fix: safe mode must carry over owner_user_ids and kill_switch_reset (or fail closed). Together with config-bounds-only-in-python, an easy trigger is the first analysis's own §0.4 advice: raising min_sleep_minutes to 180 while wake_interval_minutes stays at 60 (the live values) causes safe mode.

Smaller items, not raised as findings:
- GET /api/site/download records the download before the zip is delivered. An interrupted download still marks the site 'up to date' for the plan's WEBSITE section.
- Threat model: every Ingress app shares Home Assistant's origin. A script-running page from another app, or Home Assistant itself, can call Ember's API with the X-Ember-Request header and the owner's session. This is inherent to Ingress, and it is why the site preview's sandbox matters.
- Knock-out lifts are keyed by venture and rule, not by the case numbers the owner saw. A later, worse case keeps the lift. This belongs to the ventures area.
- wake_on_decision also fires for knock-out lifts, unlock saves and take-back, so each click can cost a cycle ($0.36-0.82 live).

Not checked in depth: how the Supervisor handles duplicate X-Remote-User-Id headers (I relied on the first analysis), and the page on a phone (target=_blank previews may lose the Ingress cookie in the companion app).
